messages:
erica: kicked off a small canary for INT8 KV cache on h100-pool at 10:05. baseline = fp32-kv. noticed decode perplexity jump on long-chat evals :thinking_face:
noah: what magnitude? numbers? :eyes:
erica: short-run numbers: avg latency +3ms, p95 +12ms, memory -42% on KV buffers. BUT decode-quality (ROUGE / perplexity) on our long prompts (8k tokens) increased ~4.8% perplexity vs baseline. small sample though. logs attached below.
ram: can you paste the exact kernel choices? maybe fallback to FP8 for some layers?
erica: perf-bot shows kernel selection: mixed-quant kernels: first 20 layers -> int8-gemmfast, layers 21-40 -> fp8-emul fallback, decode runtime kernel selector hit a mixed path. config used: `kv_quant=INT8`, `calib_mode=per_tensor`, `batch_hint=auto`, `max_batch=16`.
ciara: calibration set was our 512-token dev set, right? that explains drift on 8k sequences. calibrating on short contexts underestimates kv range for long runs.
eroica: yep. created the calib snapshot from mobile-chat logs (mostly <512).
noah: two quick ideas: 1) re-run calibration with longer context samples (2 to 8k) and per-channel scaling. 2) force kernel routing to prefer fp8 for attention-kv decode while keeping int8 for weights. tradeoffs: 1) more accurate dynamic range -> quality restored, 2) possible perf hit at p95 due to extra fp8 path.
ram: also check KV packing layout alignment — int8 kernels we use assume 128-byte alignment, misaligned KV can cause slowdowns or unexpected fallback. CIARA, can you dump the allocator traces?
ciara: dumping now. allocator shows frequent 256B allocations then 64B fragments; looks like our prefix-caching path fragments memory under high concurrency.
erica: interesting — memory fragmentation could push the runtime into slower placement and kernel fallback. that could explain tail latency + decode regressions.
noah: for immediate canary rollback, what do we want? rollback kv_quant change or restrict to non-chat routes?
erica: suggested plan: (1) pause rollout for chat-long route, (2) run a focused calibration job with representative long-context traces + per-channel scales, (3) add a temporary routing rule: if seq_len > 2k -> use fp32/fp8 KV path. also schedule microbenchmarks for aligned vs misaligned KV layouts.
ram: agree. also add a perf test that simulates concurrent small writes to the prefix cache (mimic PLG burst writes) — we saw fragmentation only under concurrent small prefixes.
ciara: created a repro script: ```bash
# repro long-chat decode with int8-kv
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_POOL=h100-canary
python tools/run_decode.py --model redwood-v1 --kv-quant INT8 --calib-mode per_tensor --input tests/long_chat_sample.json --batch 4
```
erica: great. I'll collect traces, flamegraphs and flame-timeline for kernels. can someone run a quick kernel-ops profiler? perf-bot: scheduled kernel-profiler job #4522 on h100-canary, ETA 25m.
noah: if calibration + packing fixes restore quality, we can re-enable with a staged rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and monitor perplexity + tail latency. add automated rollback if p95 delta > 10ms or perplexity delta > 2%.
erica: adding alerts now to rollout policy. also toggling `batch_hint=prefer_small` for chat-long to reduce prefix fragmentation in interim.
ram: one more note: int8->fp8 transitions during decode can cause small numeric inconsistencies in KV accumulation; add a deterministic seed check in eval harness to detect nondeterministic drift.
erica: noted. I'll run the eval harness overnight with long-context calib and per-channel scaling. will report back tomorrow. thanks all :pray:
deploy-bot: canary paused by erica at 10:42 (reason: decode quality regression on long-chat).``
